text:
ravi: RFC follow-up: proposing we split eviction responsibilities into Allocator (global ranking + issuance) and Owner (local apply + safety). dropping a short prototyping plan here so we can debate edgecases.

anya: quick why-split question: what's the upside versus single controller?

ravi: main gains: unblocks global heuristics (hotset/windowed scoring) without forcing owners to implement them; reduces owner surface area, easier testing for owner implementations. also easier to A/B allocator heuristics.

drew: correctness concern: how do we avoid lost or duplicated evicts when allocator and owner disagree or on crashes?

kai: idea: allocator issues immutable "evict-token" with fields: prefix, lease_epoch, token_id, expires_at, and HMAC(signature). owner only accepts tokens with valid HMAC and matching lease_epoch. owner performs a CAS on prefix metadata before making demote/evict change. if CAS fails we NACK.

anya: so owner-only CAS provides a linearization point. what about the case where owner ACKs but crashes before applying? allocator thinks it's applied.

ravi: owner writes a small durable pending-journal entry before ACK. sequence: 1) alloc sends token, 2) owner validates & persist pending{token_id, prefix, intent}, 3) owner ACKs to alloc, 4) owner applies CAS demote/evict, 5) owner clears pending. on restart, reconciler inspects pending entries and fixes.

drew: how does allocator track outstanding tokens? does it keep per-prefix state?

kai: allocator keeps lightweight outstanding-token index (token_id -> node). it's not the source of truth for final state, just a coordination hint. Reconciler job cross-checks allocator index and owner journals for stray tokens past TTL.

marta: SRE note: reconciler must run at bounded QPS and support backoff to avoid thundering herd when many tokens expire. include jitter + token-scoped linear backoff.

anya: race about idempotency: what if reconciler retriggers same token twice? owner ops must be idempotent keyed by token_id. apply/demote logic should be no-op if already applied.

ravi: agreed. action_id/token_id must be unique and enforced in owner journal so replays skip.

drew: test vectors we should run: inject crash between ACK and apply; inject corrupted HMAC; simulate mismatched lease_epoch; simulate allocator GC of stale tokens.

kai: rollout plan: feature-flag allocator issuance, owner-side acceptance guarded behind gate. start with soft-demote mode: token causes only priority-lowering rather than immediate eviction. soft-demote reduces blast radius while exercising codepaths.

sre-bot: canary-schedule: rollout/evict-split v0.1 -> nodeset small-canary-2 at sha:deadbeef.

marta: metrics to monitor: token_issue_rate, token_ack_latency, owner_pending_count, reconcile_fix_rate, prefix_misread_rate, cross-node-stale-reads. add alert if prefix_misread_rate > 0 for 5m.

anya: config knobs: token_TTL, reconciler_interval, owner_pending_retention, soft-demote-window. we should default conservative values.

drew: one more subtlety: what if allocator reassigns token to different node after TTL and new node applies? could that conflict with owner journal from previous node?

ravi: owner journal is global per-prefix (owner writes to its local durable store), but reconciler enforces single-apply by comparing token_id and lease_epoch. allocator should avoid reissuing same prefix token with identical lease_epoch; reissue requires incremented lease_epoch. that prevents split-brain.

kai: formal checklist for PR: token schema + HMAC validation, owner pending-journal CRUD + idempotency guard, CAS demote/apply path, reconciler (read allocator index + owner journals), soft-demote flag + metrics, canary rollout doc.

marta: ops SOP: if reconciler reports >5% stuck tokens after 10min, pause allocator issuance and run manual reconcile.

ravi: I'll prototype token issuance + owner journal this week and open a draft PR. pairing with @drew on the correctness notes. thanks for the quick feedback.

anya: :+1: keep the tests small and deterministic.

drew: +1, also add a chaos test that replays journal entries out of order.

kai: thumbs up.

sre-bot: note: next steps ticket created: INF-evict-split-2024; assign ravi,drew.
